final_output:
70% of top AI researchers have never worked on a product that shipped to 100M users. Andrej Karpathy just did.

Karpathy’s move to Anthropic’s pre-training team isn’t just another hiring splash. It’s a signal that the next leap in LLMs won’t come from scaling compute alone—it’ll come from rethinking how we pretrain. He’s building a team to push Claude’s pretraining efficiency, not just its size. [S4]

Why this matters for students: Karpathy’s work at Tesla and OpenAI proved that raw scale isn’t enough. His focus now is on *data quality*, *curriculum design*, and *model efficiency*—the kind of problems that separate research from engineering. [S2]

Expect Anthropic to open-source more pretraining tools. Karpathy’s public talks emphasize reproducibility. If his team ships a new pretraining framework, expect it to drop as a reference implementation for researchers. [S3]

The bet: Karpathy thinks the next 2–3 years at the frontier of LLMs will be defined by *how* we train, not *how much* we train. If he’s right, Anthropic’s approach could force OpenAI and others to rethink their pretraining stacks. [S1]

What to watch: Will Anthropic publish benchmarks showing Claude’s pretraining efficiency gains? If yes, expect a wave of PhD students and startups to fork their work.
